text:
emma_support: heads up — AcmeAnalytics opened an escalation. After today's v3.2 canary rollout, their agents are getting toolcall schema errors when calling the `geocode` tool. Only started after canary. Customer sample attached below.

emma_support: error snippet from our exec-api logs: `422 schema_validation_failed: unknown field 'user_timezone' in args`

emma_support: example payload they sent:
```json
{
  "tool": "geocode",
  "args": {"address": "1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy", "user_timezone": "PDT"}
}
```

jordan_eng: thanks emma — can you paste the request_id and the model_variant selected for those requests?

emma_support: request_id=4a7d9c11, I see `model_variant: rdw:base/v3.2` in the trace. Customer claims no changes on their side.

deploy-bot: rollout v3.2 canary started 2391233000 (10% traffic), health checks passed until 2391233600, observed increased 422 spikes.

maria_sre: quick hypothesis: v3.2 tightened toolcall arg validation. Previously we were permissive and stripped unknown fields before passing to tool schemas; v3.2 appears to be emitting a new `user_timezone` field and the RPC layer is now failing strict schema validation.

kyle_prod: reproduced locally — when model_variant v3.2 is chosen, the tool router maps to `geocode-v2` which expects `{"address","region"}` only. The model now adds `user_timezone` in args. Runtime validation returns unknown-field -> 422.

sophia_support: customer impact: several production jobs failing (batch geocoding). They want either a rollback or a hotfix. Their legal/product teams are waiting.

jordan_eng: mitigation options: 1) make the tool schema permissive to allow extra fields (quick but risky), 2) strip unknown fields in the RPC layer before schema validation (safer short-term), 3) pin affected tenants to v3.1 while we fix model behavior. Thoughts?

maria_sre: I prefer option 2 + tenant pin as a second line. Option 1 could mask other bugs.

kyle_prod: I can push a temporary RPC-layer sanitizer that drops unknown keys for geocode calls within the tenant scope. ETA ~90 minutes if we do a hotfix canary. Alternatively, roll back the v3.2 canary to v3.1 for the entire canary cohort. Which does support want?

emma_support: customer is asking for rollback to v3.1 for their tenant only — they want immediate mitigation and a permanent fix later.

jordan_eng: we have per-tenant routing. Maria, can you apply routing rule: `tenant:acme -> model:rdw:base/v3.1`? That should be quick and avoids full rollback.

maria_sre: doing it now. Command: `rdw routes set --tenant acme --model rdw:base/v3.1 --scope tenant --comment "mitigate geocode schema break"`

maria_sre: route applied at 2391234400. Confirmed 200 OK for subsequent requests from acme tenant.

deploy-bot: rollback request acknowledged at 2391234500. Canary rollback to v3.1 for canary cohort scheduled (if org wants broader rollback, please confirm).

kyle_prod: I'll still prep the RPC sanitizer patch as a fallback in case other customers surface similar unknown fields.

sophia_support: I'll update AcmeOps: "We've pinned your tenant to v3.1 and are preparing a fix; no action required on your side. We'll follow up with a postmortem." :pray: 

emma_support: please collect a few more failing traces (request_ids) from the customer so we can correlate which model outputs added the field.

jordan_eng: noted. Also filing a bug to the model onboarding team: `model-onboard-4678` — v3.2 introduced extra tool arg emission for `geocode`. We need model-side fix or explicit mapping to accepted schema.

sophia_support: customer replied: "thanks, pin worked, jobs resuming." I'll keep thread open until sanitizer or model fix shipped.

emma_support: closing loop here but leaving thread for follow-ups. TL;DR: per-tenant pin to v3.1 applied, canary rollback ready if needed, RPC sanitizer being prepared as fallback.
